adoption.rationale: The pinned code independently documents Markdown injection escaping for report text, exposes optional third-party YARA rules, parses author metadata through authorWithURLRe and url.Parse, and places the stored author URL in a Markdown link. A full YARA-X-to-report.Generate-to-Markdown replay reproduced a second attacker-chosen HTTPS link. The contract is a counterexample-finding question; the regex model alone is not treated as proof of the output effect.

contract.declared_domain: Counterexample domain: one-line ASCII YARA author metadata that matches the Go RE2 search expression, whose captured URL is accepted by net/url.Parse, with a non-prefix reference URL so the later author-URL compatibility branch does not replace the capture. Product reachability is checked by compiling a valid YARA rule, matching a sentinel, calling the exact pinned report.Generate and Markdown renderer with YARA-X 1.19.0. The solver fixes one concrete witness; it does not establish safety for all metadata or downstream Markdown viewers.
contract.guarantee: Third-party YARA author metadata accepted by the pinned authorWithURLRe and Go URL parser must not close the generated Markdown author link or add a second hyperlink in Malcontent's Markdown report.
contract.input_source: The author metadata value from an operator-enabled third-party YARA rule, read through Malcontent's RuleFS and parsed into a report behavior.

domain: The pinned authorWithURLRe search capture must not permit source metadata to close its Markdown link and add a second external link
name: MC-malcontent-author-metadata-extra-markdown-link
